figures.caption_en: Eight named events Kenyans remember, 1982–2024, one lane each; a bar spans the event's months, and colour is the phase the list assigns — El Niño, La Niña, positive IOD. Hover a band for its one-line story. **Only these eight are named — an unmarked year is not a calm one.** National: the county and shared controls do not change it.
figures.about_en:
**This is an editorial layer, not a data series.** The eight events come from `events.json`, a small file authored for this notebook — no upstream dataset, no `.meta.json`, no licence to cite. Each entry carries a name, a start and an end month, a phase label, a one-line story, and the seasons it claims. Nothing here is computed, and no number should be read off it: the measured driver values live in Figure 2.1 (hover its strips for the raw index value) and the season counts in Figure 2.2.

One row per event, oldest at the top, so no two labels collide. A bar runs from the event's start month to its end month, so **its length is the window someone drew around the event, not its severity**; the colour is the file's `phase` field — El Niño, La Niña, positive IOD — not an intensity, and the figure carries no colour key (the phase is spelled out in the event's name or story, and is a column in the download). The x-axis is fixed from January 1981 to January 2027 whatever the events cover — the earliest band starts September 1982, the latest ends May 2024. Hovering gives the event name and its blurb; the download gives event, start, end, phase and story.

**The phase labels are editorial judgements and can disagree with the notebook's own classification.** The file's note says the windows were drawn against the driver-index thresholds the notebook computes rather than typed-in values, but the fit is loose at the margins: OND 2005 sits exactly on the −0.50 RONI threshold, so the page-wide classifier reads it Neutral while this figure paints the 2005–06 band La Niña; MAM 2017, inside the 2016–17 band, is ENSO-neutral (RONI −0.09); and 1997–98 was both a record El Niño and a strongly positive IOD (DMI +1.01) yet carries a single colour. Where the two differ, the computed classification on Figures 2.1 and 2.2 is the one to trust.

Coverage is deliberately thin: **four La Niña droughts, three El Niños and one positive-IOD event — the ones people name, not the only bad seasons Kenya has had.** Read a blank stretch as "no named event", never as a settled or calm period. Each event also tags the seasons it claims (14 in all — 10 OND and 4 MAM, OND-1982 through OND-2023); those tags are what put an event name beside a year on the season-lens chips and the outlook analogue chips, and whether a named La Niña event ended within about three years of the data edge switches one line of the outlook's "leaning wetter" advice. **The driver shading on every other chart is computed from the indices, not taken from this list.**

**Data:** curated named-event list (`data/KE-enso-explorer/events.json`), editorial — no licence. The indices the names refer to are NOAA CPC (Niño 3.4 / RONI), Met Office HadISST extended with NOAA PSL ERSST (DMI/IOD) and the derived Western-V. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

figures.caption_en: Each dot is one year's season-mean greenness (NDVI) for the county, as a percentage of normal, grouped by that season's driver — OND (short rains) by ENSO + IOD, MAM (long rains) by the Western-V — at 1 and 1.5 standard deviations. Black ticks are group medians. **Groups can rest on as few as two years.** A toggle hides the MAM panel.
figures.about_en:
Vegetation condition is WFP VAM's *Kenya: NDVI at Subnational Level* (MODIS collection 6.1, Terra+Aqua) from HDX, CC-BY, joined to the 47 counties through the OCHA admin boundaries. WFP publishes on sub-county units, so the county value is a pixel-weighted roll-up and % of normal is recomputed from the rolled-up values (NDVI ÷ WFP's long-term mean for that 10-day period × 100), never averaged from the sub-units. A dot is the plain mean of that season's nine 10-day values for the county you have selected — a mean of ratios, not a season-total ratio. The record starts July 2002, so each panel holds 24 seasons: OND 2002–2025, MAM 2003–2026, the same seasons for every county.

Each panel keeps its season's driver whatever the driver selectors elsewhere in the notebook are set to. OND uses the combined ENSO + IOD state: the relative Niño index (RONI) for the concurrent OND season and the Dipole Mode Index (HadISST, coalesced with ERSST so recent seasons are not left blank — HadISST stops in April 2025, so OND 2025's DMI is ERSST throughout), each standardised on 1991–2020, averaged, then re-standardised on 1991–2020; the DMI season needs all three of October–December or the year is dropped. MAM uses the standardised Western-V (WNP) index for Mar–May, again with all three months required — no partial seasons. A season is strong at 1.5 sd or more, moderate from 1 to 1.5, otherwise neutral/weak; the hover label goes one step finer, separating weak from neutral at 0.5 sd. Dot colour is the same ±2 sd strength ramp used for the chart backgrounds. Because the drivers are ocean indices and the NDVI record covers all 47 counties identically, the grouping is the same for every county — changing county moves the dots up and down, never between bands. A year whose driver index is incomplete is dropped from the panel and kept in the CSV as "no index"; a panel with fewer than five usable years is replaced by a note instead of a chart.

Limits. Bands holding no seasons are not drawn, so an absent band means the record holds no season of that strength — it is never a low value: as it stands OND has two strong El Niño/+IOD seasons (2015, 2023) and no strong La Niña/−IOD season, and MAM has two strong high-Western-V seasons (2021, 2025) and no low-Western-V band at all — not one of the 24 long rains reached −1 sd. **A median drawn on two or three dots describes those years, not a relationship** — and unlike Figure 2.2 this figure does not fade or star thin groups, so read the year labels. Greenness also answers temperature, grazing pressure, land use and the previous season's carry-over, and it follows rain with a lag of weeks, so the grouping shows association, never attribution.

**Data:** WFP VAM subnational NDVI (MODIS, via HDX; CC-BY) on OCHA COD admin boundaries; drivers NOAA CPC (RONI), HadISST via NOAA PSL coalesced with ERSST (DMI), Western-V derived from ERSSTv5 after Funk et al. (2018). [Methods & sources →](#methods)

figures.caption_en: The county's drought index (SPEI) at the window you choose — 3, 6 or 12 months. Sustained values below −1 mark entrenched drought, below −2 exceptional drought. **The line breaks every December: that window is quarantined, not dry.** Background shading tracks the driver control above in standard deviations, not SPEI units; dashed outlines mark the seasons matching the lens.
figures.about_en:
County drought index (SPEI), pre-extracted as admin1 zonal means via the Atlas climate hub and served in `chirps_county.parquet`. It arrives already standardised from the producer and the notebook re-fits nothing, so the curve is raw SPEI and 0 is that window's 1991–2020 normal.

**What is plotted.** The parquet serves twelve overlapping 3-month windows per year, each labelled by the year it *ends* in (DJF 2024 = Dec 2023 – Feb 2024). Annual rows are dropped and each window is drawn at its centre month — DJF at January, MAM at April, OND at November — one point per month, December excepted, with dashed rules at −1 and −2 and the negative area filled. SPEI-3 and SPEI-6 start in 1981 (first complete windows centred April and July), SPEI-12 in January 1982; all three run to the most recent served window, centred March 2026.

**December is quarantined.** The NDJ window is served, but the producer builds it from Nov(Y) + Dec(Y−1) + Jan(Y) — a year-label shift applied to December only, mixing two different short-rains seasons (checked against the monthly county file: that recipe reproduces the served NDJ exactly, the correct end-labelled one does not). Its 1991–2020 spread is deflated to match — 0.60 sd on SPEI-3, against 0.75–0.89 for every other window. The chart therefore excludes NDJ outright and cuts the line wherever consecutive points fall more than 45 days apart; with a county driver the December background is unpainted for the same reason. **The December gap is a withheld measurement, not a dry month.** A producer-side fix is pending.

**Backgrounds.** These come from the shared §3 driver controls — linked across every §3 figure, so changing one changes them all — not from SPEI. Continuous paints every month with its own **measured** rolling 3-month window, standardised per calendar month over 1991–2020: nothing is interpolated, and nothing is painted where a window is missing or beyond the last measured month. Discrete paints only the measured OND/MAM season windows, binned into classes (untinted below 1 sd, then moderate and strong). County drivers are re-standardised against their own 1991–2020 record, because a county-mean SPEI is variance-compressed by spatial averaging (0.49–0.94 sd per window, not 1) — so shade depth and curve depth are different scales, and the ramp saturates at ±2 sd. The county SPEI-3 driver with the 3-month window selected just repeats the curve behind itself; pick an ocean driver to read drought against ENSO/IOD state. Discrete OND blocks classify ENSO with RONI, the monthly view with the plain Niño 3.4 window, and the two can disagree: OND 2024 is a weak La Niña by RONI (−0.80 sd) but reads Neutral month by month (−0.25 to −0.43 sd). Western-V is a long-rains (MAM) control and always shows discrete season blocks.

**Limits.** County averaging smooths sub-county extremes, so −1 here can hide worse locally. SPEI is a standardised water balance — rainfall minus evaporative demand — so a hot year deepens the deficit with no change in rain. The windows are not interchangeable: −1 on SPEI-3 is one failed season, −1 on SPEI-12 a year of accumulated deficit. Nothing here is a forecast.

**Data:** CHIRPS v3 precipitation + CHIRTS-ERA5 temperature → SPEI (UCSB Climate Hazards Center, CC-BY; admin1 zonal via the Atlas climate hub); background drivers NOAA Niño 3.4 / RONI and HadISST–ERSST DMI. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

figures.caption_en: Ten-day NDVI as a percentage of that dekad's long-term normal (WFP VAM, 2002–present): below 100 (orange) is a vegetation deficit, above 100 (green) greener than usual. Each selected county gets its own panel and y-axis — compare shape, not height. Background shades the chosen driver's strength, blank where no window is measured; it and the dashed outlines follow the page's county.
figures.about_en:
WFP VAM "Kenya: NDVI at Subnational Level" (MODIS collection 6.1, Terra+Aqua) from HDX, CC-BY; county names from the OCHA Kenya Common Operational Dataset. WFP publishes on the legacy sub-county grid, where the admin2 p-code's first five characters are the county, so no name matching is guessed. A county-dekad is the **pixel-weighted** (n_pixels) rollup of its sub-units' NDVI and of WFP's own long-term mean for that dekad-of-year, and the anomaly is then recomputed as NDVI ÷ long-term mean × 100 — **never an average of sub-unit percentages**. The baseline is WFP's, not refitted here, so this figure shows condition against normal, not any long-term greening or browning trend. Coverage is complete: all 47 counties × 864 dekads, 2002-07-01 to 2026-06-21 (40,608 rows, no county-dekad unreported), and the pixel count behind each county is identical in every dekad, so no sub-unit is ever silently dropped. 2002 and 2026 are part-years, 18 dekads each.

Each selected county gets its own panel. Panels share one time axis, but every panel's y-axis is fitted to that county's own range (always at least 90–110), so a deep-looking trough in a stable county is not the same fall as in a volatile one. The CSV download carries only the counties currently selected.

Background and outlines are the section's linked controls — change them at any figure in Section 3 and every figure follows. Everything is standardised against **1991–2020**. The strength words in the tooltips are neutral below 0.5 sd, weak 0.5–1, moderate 1–1.5, strong 1.5 sd or more, but the shading is not banded that way: *Continuous* is a smooth ramp saturating at ±2 sd, while *Discrete* deliberately leaves anything below 1 sd untinted (the evidence bins of Figure 2.2), so a season the tooltip calls "weak" shows as blank there. *Discrete* paints only the measured OND / MAM three-month windows and nothing between them; *Continuous* paints each month with a measured, centred three-month window standardised per calendar month, so a December is only compared with other Decembers. Nothing is interpolated and nothing is painted where a window is incomplete — the centred windows stop one month short of the last monthly index (last complete window May 2026, index data to June 2026), so the most recent dekads of NDVI sit over blank background.

Two documented deviations. With the ENSO (Niño 3.4) driver the OND season blocks classify with RONI while the monthly view uses plain Niño 3.4 — no monthly RONI is served — and the two can disagree outright: OND 2024 is −0.80 sd on RONI (weak La Niña) but −0.25, −0.33 and −0.43 sd for October, November and December (Neutral). Under the default ENSO + IOD driver the gap is smaller (−0.90 sd for the season against −0.35 / −0.63 / −0.86 sd monthly). And Western-V is a long-rains-only control, so it always falls back to discrete MAM blocks.

Dashed outlines mark seasons whose CHIRPS rainfall fell in the chosen tercile of 1991–2020 **for the county selected at the top of the page**; in multi-county mode the identical outlines are drawn over every panel, so read them against that county, not each panel's. The same applies to the background when the driver is one of the two county drivers (season rainfall, SPEI-3); the four ocean drivers are national and identical for every county.

Limits: NDVI is greenness, not biomass, forage quality or livestock condition, and a county mean blends rangeland, cropland and forest in one number — a large county's average can hide a local failure. County means also rest on very unequal pixel counts, from about 2,300 for Marsabit down to 10 for Mombasa and 19 for Vihiga, so the smallest counties are the least robust. Dekadal MODIS composites remain sensitive to cloud and aerosol contamination.

**Data:** WFP VAM NDVI (MODIS 6.1) via HDX, CC-BY; county boundaries OCHA Kenya COD; rainfall CHIRPS county series; drivers NOAA/HadISST/derived. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

figures.caption_en: IPC food-insecurity phase for the county's **worst-classified area** (FEWS NET Current Situation, 2011–2026); phase 3 is Crisis, 4 Emergency. In Steps the phase holds until reclassified — steps, not slopes — and IPC colour bands show only when the background is Off. Yearly bars give each year's worst; rounds are irregular (one in 2025). Controls set the view and background.
figures.about_en:
FEWS NET / IPC area classifications, staged as `ipc_county` (FEWS NET, public; fetched July 2026). The figure plots **only the Current Situation scenario** — the file's Near Term and Medium Term projections are neither drawn nor downloaded. Each point is `max_phase`: **the worst phase among the mapped IPC areas making up the county**, not a county-wide phase, so a Crisis step means at least one area was classified Crisis, not the whole county. 49 Current Situation rounds cover all 47 counties from Jan 2011 to Feb 2026 — four a year to 2015, three a year 2016–2024, then **one round in 2025 (October) and one so far in 2026 (February)**. The record's one long hole — **no assessment between Oct 2024 and Oct 2025** — can only be drawn in Steps as a flat twelve-month run, and the last two yearly bars each rest on a single assessment. The number of areas per county follows FEWS NET's own geography and changes over the record (1–3 areas in the two 2011 rounds, 4–27 from Jul 2011, 4–47 from Jun 2016), so early and late years are not strictly like-for-like.

**Steps** draws step-after between assessments: the phase holds at its last classification until the next round, and nothing is drawn before the first or after the last assessment — a flat run is a classification carried forward, not a measurement. **Yearly bars** take the maximum over the assessments in a calendar year, so a year with one bad round reads the same as a year with three. The dashed rule sits at phase 3, the Crisis threshold. Phase 5 (Famine) has never been classified in this record — nor in the unplotted projections; the worst observed is phase 4 (Emergency), reached in 10 of the 47 counties, while 24 counties have reached phase 3 or worse at least once.

Two shadings on one panel would multiply into unreadable colour, so in Steps the horizontal IPC phase bands are drawn **only when Background is Off**; switch a driver background on and the phase reading moves to the axis labels and the tooltip. Yearly bars keep their IPC bar colours either way — the driver sits behind them. Backgrounds standardise the chosen driver over **1991–2020**: Discrete paints the measured OND (short rains) / MAM (long rains) 3-month windows; Continuous paints each month that has a complete measured centred 3-month window — nothing is interpolated, nothing is painted beyond the last measured month, and **an unpainted month means no measured window, not a neutral one** (the county rainfall and SPEI-3 drivers have no December window, so Decembers stay blank). Yearly bars have no month axis, so there Continuous still paints OND/MAM half-slots, only with the full colour ramp instead of binned strength classes. Western-V is a MAM-only control and always shows season blocks. One nuance: OND ENSO season blocks classify with RONI while the monthly view uses the plain Niño 3.4 window, and the two can disagree — with ENSO (Niño 3.4) selected, OND 2024 is a weak La Niña at −0.8 sd by RONI but reads Neutral month by month (−0.25 to −0.43 sd). Dashed outlines mark the seasons matching the season lens (only once a lens tercile is chosen), and the lens and background controls are the section's linked set — changing them here changes every driver-shaded figure; the Steps / Yearly bars radio is local to this figure.

IPC phase is an assessed consensus classification, not a measurement, and it responds to conflict, markets and displacement as well as to rainfall — a Crisis step over a shaded La Niña season is alignment, not attribution. The CSV download is this county's Current Situation series only (reporting date + worst phase).

**Data:** FEWS NET / IPC (`ipc_county`); drivers NOAA Niño 3.4 + RONI, HadISST/ERSST DMI, derived Western-V; county rainfall and SPEI-3 from CHIRPS. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

figures.caption_en: Kilograms of maize one goat buys each month: the county's median goat price divided by its median maize price. The dashed line is the county's long-term median; **a gap in the line means months with no price report, never a fall to zero.** Quarterly and Yearly bars average the monthly ratios, and the background controls above are linked.
figures.about_en:
Both series are FEWS NET Data Warehouse (FDW) retail prices, public data. For each month the code takes the **county median across every monitored market** of the goat price (Goats, local quality, per head) and of the maize price (Maize grain, white, per kg), then divides one by the other; a month is plotted only where both series report. Goats are monitored in a single market in 19 of the 20 counties that carry the series (Isiolo has two) and maize in up to six, so on the goat side one market effectively stands for the whole county — and only 20 of Kenya's 47 counties carry a goat series at all. The plotted record runs January 2008 to May 2026, and back to January 2000 in Garissa; 18 of the 20 counties are missing May–July 2020. Gaps of one or two months are still bridged by a straight segment — the line breaks only where consecutive reported months are more than 100 days apart, that is three or more missing months. Quarterly and Yearly bars are the mean of the monthly ratios in the bucket — **not a ratio of averaged prices** — with the month count in the tooltip; a bucket running past the last reported month is drawn faded and labelled incomplete. The dashed line is the median of every monthly ratio in that county's own record, not a fixed baseline, and it stays the monthly median under the bar views. Background shading is the chosen driver's strength standardised over 1991–2020, and nothing is interpolated or painted beyond the last measured month: Discrete paints the OND (short rains) / MAM (long rains) season blocks and, for the ENSO drivers, classifies OND with RONI; Continuous paints every month with its own measured rolling 3-month window on the plain Niño3.4 index. The two can disagree in what they name — OND 2024 is a weak La Niña by RONI (−0.8 sd) but its months read Neutral (−0.25 to −0.43 sd) — though discrete blocks only take colour from 1 sd, so a weak season stays untinted in either view. Western-V, a MAM-only control, always shows season blocks, and dashed outlines mark the seasons matching the season lens. Both prices are nominal, so inflation largely cancels in the ratio, but animal condition is not recorded: in a drought a falling ratio mixes thinner animals with dearer cereal, and this figure cannot separate the two.

**Data:** FEWS NET (FDW retail market prices); drivers NOAA / HadISST / derived. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

figures.caption_en: County-tagged humanitarian reports per year, stacked by hazard. Bars count **reports filed, not impact** — reporting follows attention as much as severity, and the last two years are thinly harvested. Multi-hazard reports count once, under the first match drought → flood → epidemic → other. Background = driver strength in each year's MAM/OND half-slots; dashed outlines = the lens seasons; controls are linked.
figures.about_en:
County-tagged humanitarian and situation reports from **UN OCHA ReliefWeb**, harvested through the ReliefWeb API under a registered project appname (`steward-cgiar-aaa-atlas-enso-…`; OCHA terms of use). One banked snapshot, fetched 9 July 2026: 15,736 report–county rows from 6,715 reports by 306 publishing organisations, all 47 counties, 3 Jan 2010 – 24 Jun 2026. The chart starts at 2010 because the harvest does — nothing earlier is being hidden.

Rows are matched to your county on a normalised name (case, hyphens and apostrophes ignored; all 47 spellings match, so no county is silently empty), counted by the calendar year of the report date, and each report gets **one colour, by first match: Drought → Flood (which also catches Flash Flood) → Epidemic → Other**. That rule hides a lot: 6,956 rows carry more than one hazard tag (up to 12 on one report), 2,297 tagged Drought *and* Flood stack as Drought, and of the 3,249 rows tagged Epidemic only 308 are drawn as Epidemic — the rest are absorbed, mostly by Drought. Read the drought band as a ceiling, the flood and epidemic bands as floors. Across all 15,736 rows the rule gives 75.7% Drought, 13.3% Other, 9.1% Flood, 2.0% Epidemic; Other is 1,757 rows with no hazard tag at all plus 330 whose only tags have no colour here (308 of them insect infestation — most insect, landslide and mudslide tags vanish into Drought or Flood instead, not into Other). A report attaches to every county it is tagged to — 2.34 counties on average, 39 at most — so one national drought report lifts many counties' bars at once, though within a county each report appears exactly once. County attachment happens upstream in `impacts/reliefweb_pipeline.py`, not yet in this repo (open action 2 in DATA.md), so it cannot be re-derived from the served file. The "Most recent reports" expander lists the county's five newest, linked to the originals on reliefweb.int.

Limits: **report volume measures reporting, not impact** — it follows appeals, media cycles and agency presence, so counts are not a severity ranking between counties (Nairobi carries the most rows, 1,558, ahead of Turkana 1,272 and Marsabit 1,114; Murang'a has 9 — too few to read a shape into). The recent end is thin: 2025 is a complete year but holds 94 reports (285 rows) against 403 (1,008) in 2024, and 2026 stops at the 24 June snapshot with 42 (191). Treat the last two bars as a floor, not a fall in hazard. Background strengths are standardised on 1991–2020 (Discrete bins the intensity classes, Continuous uses the full colour ramp; a single-season driver such as Western-V shades only its MAM half-slot) — the shading and the dashed outlines line reports up against driver state, they attribute nothing.

**Data:** UN OCHA ReliefWeb (ReliefWeb API, county-tagged reports); driver indices NOAA/HadISST/derived. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

figures.caption_en: Quantity of the selected product imported into Kenya per year, stacked by partner country, in the product's unit (FEWS NET border monitoring; informal flows are field estimates, summed with formal). **A missing bar can be a recorded zero or no monitoring — the chart cannot tell them apart**; years with no records are skipped. National data — the same for every county.
figures.about_en:
FEWS NET's East Africa Cross-Border Trade (XBT) monitoring banks a monthly quantity per partner, direction, trade type and product for consignments seen at **8 Kenyan border posts** (Taveta, Moyale, Namanga, Isebania, Malaba, Lunga Lunga, Lwakhaka, Loitoktok), so **this is a national / border-post layer, not a county one** — changing the county selection does nothing to it. The staging script (`_sources/parse_xbt.py`) keeps Kenya-touching flows only (destination Kenya → Import, source Kenya → Export; transit dropped, as are rows with an unmapped partner or an unparsable quantity) and passes the banked quantity through verbatim — nothing is modelled, rescaled or gap-filled. This figure sums the Import rows for the product you pick by partner and calendar year, formal and informal together.

**Units are never mixed.** 8 of the 99 products are banked in more than one unit (refined vegetable oil in both litres and kilograms), so the chart keeps only the unit with the largest total quantity for that product — counting exports too — and drops every other row: 18 import rows in all, and for watermelon every import row, which leaves that product's chart empty. Kilograms are drawn as kilotonnes (1 kt = 1,000,000 kg); livestock stay in head (the axis prints the raw code, "ea"), oils in litres.

**Why a gap is ambiguous.** Two-thirds of the record — 15,966 of 24,272 rows — is an explicit zero, so a partner-year that sums to zero draws a zero-height, invisible bar: for Maize Grain (White), Uganda is a recorded zero in 2013–15 and 2018–21. Years with no rows at all get no slot on the axis rather than an empty one; 22 of the 94 products with imports have a missing year inside their own span.

Known limits: 24,272 Kenya-touching rows, 2010–2024, 99 products, 10 partners; only 20,802 rows are imports, and they arrive from five partners — Tanzania, Ethiopia and Uganda carry all but 50 rows, Malawi and Zambia the remainder. 5 products are export-only, so picking one draws nothing. Coverage is thin at the ends and uneven between: 2010 is 11 rows of Ethiopian cattle at Moyale alone, 2024 stops in September, Taveta reports only from 2012, Lunga Lunga only 2022–24, Loitoktok only 2011–12 — **a bar that falls can mean less monitoring, not less trade.** Informal volumes are field aggregations, not customs records. The source carries no price or value column, so this is quantity only and cannot be read as the value of trade.

**Data:** FEWS NET East Africa Cross-Border Trade (XBT) monitoring (FEWS NET public licence). [Methods & sources →](#methods)
defects_found: CRITICAL — the caption's bolded headline claim is false and reverses the truth. 'A year or partner with no bar was not monitored — not zero': 15,966 of 24,272 rows (65.8%) carry qty exactly 0, including 13,900 of the 20,802 Import rows. A partner-year that sums to zero draws a zero-height (invisible) bar, so blank is AMBIGUOUS, not proof of non-monitoring. On the default product itself (Maize Grain (White)) 8 of 44 partner-year cells sum to exactly zero — Uganda 2013, 2014, 2015, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 and Ethiopia 2014. Corrected to 'a recorded zero or no monitoring — the chart cannot tell them apart'.

CRITICAL — '5 of the 99 products are export-only — pick one of those and the chart is empty' undercounts the empty-chart cases. Watermelon has 3 Import rows (all kg, Tanzania/Taveta 2015) but its dominant unit is 'ea', chosen from a single 18,176-ea EXPORT row; the xbtImports filter `qty_unit = xbtUnit` therefore drops all three import rows and the chart is empty too. 6 products, not 5, render blank. (Export-only 5 confirmed: Horses and other equines, Oats (Unspecified), Wheat Grain (Food Aid), Diesel, Swine / pigs.)

The About's dominant-unit description is incomplete in the way that causes the Watermelon bug: the xbtUnit cell has NO direction filter, so the unit is picked over Imports AND Exports, and it compares SUM(qty) across incommensurable units. Draft says only 'picks each product's dominant unit by total quantity'. Added 'counting exports too' and the 18-row / Watermelon consequence.

'Monitoring starts March 2010 and ends September 2024, so the first and last bars cover 10 and 9 months, not full years' — materially misleading for 2010. The whole of 2010 is 11 rows, one product (Cattle), one partner (Ethiopia), one border point (Moyale), Mar–Dec. For 98 of the 99 products 2010 does not exist at all, so there is no '10-month 2010 bar' to caveat. Caption's '2010 and 2024 are part-years' implies near-complete coverage minus Jan–Feb. Replaced with the concrete '2010 is 11 rows of Ethiopian cattle at Moyale alone'. (2024 = 9 months, 1,779 rows, 61 products — that half is sound.)

Missing from both drafts: the Plot x channel has no type or domain (`x: {tickFormat: "d", label: null}` with Plot.barY), so it is a BAND scale — a year with no rows for the selected product gets no slot on the axis at all rather than an empty gap, and the axis silently reads as contiguous. 22 of the 94 products with imports have at least one interior missing year. Added to caption ('years with no records are skipped') and About.

'counts consignments as they cross 8 Kenyan border points' — qty is a quantity in kg / ea / L, not a count of consignments; the grain is one row per partner × direction × trade_type × product × month. Reworded to 'banks a monthly quantity per partner, direction, trade type and product'.

parse_xbt.py filtering is described incompletely: besides dropping transit/non-Kenya flows it also silently drops rows whose partner is absent from the fixed ISO3 map and rows whose qty will not parse as a float. 'nothing is modelled, rescaled or gap-filled' stands, but the drop rules do not. Added.

'livestock stay in head' — the y-axis label is `imported (${xbtUnitKt ? "kt" : xbtUnit})`, so it literally prints 'imported (ea)', never 'head'. Clarified in the About so the reader can match the prose to the axis.

Corrected caption is 60 words. It also drops the old caption's inline FEWS NET provenance; restored as a short parenthetical (plotFooter meta already prints Source/Scope, so this is belt-and-braces).

No small-n / lag / 'suggestive only' caveat existed in the old string.

DATA-DOC MISMATCH (not a caption defect, but fix before release): data/KE-enso-explorer/xbt_trade.meta.json 'coverage' lists 11 partners including Somalia; the parquet has 10 and zero Somalia rows. Somalia IS present in parse_xbt.py's ISO3 map, so it was absent from the banked CSV, not dropped by staging.
